title: Tenant-gated request gateway for hosted chat/streaming/toolcall eligibility
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Define and implement a tenant-weighted gateway that classifies inbound Hosted API feature requests (chat, streaming, tool/function calls, structured outputs) into SLA-aware lanes and onboarding eligibility buckets. Goal: reduce manual intake triage for enterprise customers, enforce security/sla gating early, and automate routing to the appropriate intake workflow (self-serve, concierge, sales-assisted). Deliver a policy DSL for mapping tenant signals (commit level, compliance flags, requested features) to routing decisions and a lightweight UI for CS/SE to override decisions.
acceptance_criteria: Policy DSL defined and documented in Confluence with examples for chat streaming and toolcalls
Automated classifier routes >= 70% of enterprise inbound requests to a correct lane in staging based on historical labeled set
Override UI implemented in Console mock and validated by CS with two enterprise customers
End-to-end onboarding path tested: incoming request -> route -> assigned intake lane -> SLA assignment
Metrics emitted: routing_decision, rule_hit_count, override_rate, mean_time_to_route
comments: 2026-01-18 - Ava Martinez: Initial intake ticket created after weekly CS sync. Key problem: too many enterprise hosted API requests require manual assessment for streaming/toolcalls and structured output SLAs. Proposed solution: rule-driven gateway + lightweight override UI.

2026-01-25 - Ravi Patel: Scoped work for MVP: (1) policy DSL proto, (2) classifier training using existing labeled backlog of 1.2k requests, (3) Console override mock. Removed full automation of billing/skus - out of scope for MVP.

2026-02-02 - Eng review (S. Nguyen): Flagged two engineering trade-offs: inline classifier vs separate microservice (we prefer microservice to isolate latency), and whether gating should block request ingestion or mark for prioritized human review. Decision: mark + prioritized human queue for first rollout to avoid false negatives blocking customers.

2026-02-09 - Design review (M. Rivera): Provided Console mockups and accessibility notes; added 'reason' and 'confidence' fields on routing cards. Follow-ups: add a compact view for SEs and a reveal panel for rule provenance.
2026-02-12 - PM note: Labeled training dataset curated (1.2k requests) and anonymized; engineering to start model experiments (recall-focused classifier). Linked dataset in Drive.

2026-02-18 - Engineering update (R. Patel): Prototype classifier achieves 74% lane-match recall on hold-out set; false-positive rate concentrated on low-commit tenants. Plan: add tenant-weight multiplier and condition on 'recent-usage' signal.

2026-02-20 - CS feedback (K. Osei): Two pilot enterprise customers reviewed the mock; both value explicit SLA mapping and manual override. CS requests audit log entries and email notifications when overrides occur.
2026-02-25 - Security review kickoff: Security team requested KMS-integrated storage for sensitive request metadata and RBAC checks on the override UI. Added to dependency list and updated scope.

2026-02-28 - PM update: Canaries targeted for 2026-03-08 in staging: (a) classifier routing only + human queue, (b) UI override visible to CS in staging. Next steps: finalize policy DSL syntax, add telemetry hooks, schedule CS pilot sessions. Assigned follow-ups to ENG and Design.
Open action items: ENG-40298 implement microservice scaffold, DES-8742 finalize mock and handoff, schedule two-seat CS pilot (week of 2026-03-08).
